questions.explanationText: Since every person faces the centre, each person's left is the anticlockwise direction and each person's right is the clockwise direction. Pinning P and applying the conditions one by one leaves exactly one possible arrangement. Working through the conditions, the clockwise seating order is P, T, S, Q, R. R faces the centre, so R's right is the clockwise direction; moving 1 seat that way from R gives P.

questions.questionText: 10 persons sit at a round table in two concentric circles. E, C, D, A, B sit in the inner circle facing outward, and H, G, F, J, I sit in the outer circle facing the centre. Each person of the inner circle sits exactly facing one person of the outer circle. Moving clockwise, the inner circle order is E, C, D, A, B, and the outer circle person facing each of them, taken in the same clockwise sequence, is H, G, F, J, I. Who faces the person sitting immediately to the left of B in the inner circle?
questions.explanationText: B faces outward, so the person immediately to B's left is one seat clockwise, namely E. The outer-circle person facing E, at the same clockwise position, is H.

options.text: Charu sits immediately to the right of Arjun

Girish and Arjun are immediate neighbours

questions.explanationText: Since every person faces the centre, each person's left is the anticlockwise direction and each person's right is the clockwise direction. Exactly 48 seating arrangements satisfy the conditions, one of them being the clockwise order Arjun, Bela, Dev, Ekta, Charu, Faiz, Girish. Each of the other statements is realised in at least one of these arrangements, but 'Charu sits immediately to the right of Arjun' is contradicted by every one of them, so it can never be true.

With 6 seats, the person opposite anyone is 3 seats away, and 3 seats from Arjun is journalist.
